candidate.answerReason: Subtracting triangles BCD and EFD from the rectangle gives 640−160−160=320, agreeing with choice A.

methods.label: Subtract the two outside triangles
methods.explanation:
The quadrilateral is what remains of the rectangle after removing triangles \(BCD\) and \(EFD\). These triangles have perpendicular sides along the rectangle, so their areas are easy to find.

Since \(B\) and \(F\) are midpoints,
\[
BC=32\div2=16,\qquad EF=20\div2=10.
\]
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so \(CD=20\) and \(ED=32\). Thus the rectangle has area \(32\cdot20=640\), while the two triangles have areas
\[
\frac{16\cdot20}{2}=160
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{10\cdot32}{2}=160.
\]
The two triangles and the quadrilateral fill the rectangle without overlapping interiors. Therefore the requested area is
\[
640-160-160=\boxed{320},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
